title: Principality of Antioch
capsule: The Principality of Antioch was a Crusader state founded in 1098 by Bohemond I of Taranto after the First Crusade's capture of Antioch (June 1098), encompassing the Orontes valley, the port of St. Symeon, and Cilician marches at its greatest extent. Its position between the County of Tripoli, the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, and the Zengid/Ayyubid states of Syria made it the most militarily pressured of the Crusader polities; it suffered catastrophic defeat at the Field of Blood (Ager Sanguinis, 1119), where regent Roger of Salerno was killed, and endured further contraction under Zengi, Nur ad-Din, and Saladin. Antioch fell to the Mamluk sultan Baybars on 18 May 1268, who described the massacre in a triumphant letter to the count of Tripoli; the dataset's terminal date of 1272 marks the effective end of the principality's viable existence, though nominal Crusader claims continued until 1275.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extent is mapped from Crusader and Islamic sources and is reasonably well established for the twelfth century; border zones with Cilician Armenia and Zengid Syria shifted frequently and precise demarcation is uncertain.
